svg.title: Where predictive uncertainty comes from
svg.desc: Three routes to an error bar - MC dropout, ensembles, a GP head on the backbone features - feeding the same variance decomposition into total, epistemic and noise terms, and the calibration questions asked of the result.

g.text: MC dropout (sampling)
keep dropout active at inference, run M passes
ConcreteDropout learns the rate, so the spread
is calibrated rather than arbitrary
trap: a dropout layer in eval mode is a silent no-op
Ensembles (sampling)
K checkpoints: deep (K trainings), snapshot (cyclic
learning rate), checkpoint (last K epochs), input
(remeshed variants); mean and std of the K outputs
trap: members can all be wrong together off-range
GP head (closed form, one pass)
backbone features -> DKL MLP -> variational GP
FieldVariationalGPHead per point, VariationalGPHead
per case; inducing points seeded from real features
trap: skip the seed / MSE / KL-ramp recipe and variance collapses

svg.text: total variance(x) = epistemic variance(x) + noise variance(x)
epistemic: what more training data would remove - rises where the surrogate extrapolates (the OOD signal)
noise: input-dependent scatter the data itself carries. Dropout and ensembles give only the first; GP heads give both.

g.text: Is it the right size? (calibration)
z = (y - mean) / std should be standard normal:
z-RMS near 1, 95 % coverage near 0.95,
low NLPD, sharpness as small as calibration allows
uncertainty_utils.ComputeCalibrationMetricValues
Does it rank the errors? (discrimination)
rank correlation between std and actual error,
sparsification curve and its area (AUSE):
dropping the most uncertain points should drop the error
ensemble crps / kcrps in ValidationMetricsProcess
Does it grow off-distribution? (OOD)
growth ratio (std_ood / std_id) / (rmse_ood / rmse_id)
near 1; below it the model is over-confident outside
its training family - which is what the OOD guard is for
ood_guard_utils, "ood_guard" block on every process
